title: M3+ earthquake rates fell, but their M2+ share had no clear change at The Geysers in 2004-2025
abstract: We tested earthquake sizes across a previously reported early-2014 rate change at The Geysers. A fixed ComCat snapshot has 3,385 M2+ events in 2004-2013 and 2,398 in 2014-2025. The M3+ rate fell from 18.5 to 11.4 per year. Its post/pre ratio was 0.617, with a conditional 95% year-resampling interval of 0.490-0.769. The M3+ share of M2+ events was 5.47% before the boundary and 5.71% after it. Its ratio was 1.045 (0.842-1.292), which gives no clear change. Two-year blocks and joint location-depth adjustment also gave share intervals that include one. This does not establish an unchanged size distribution. A descriptive size slope fell, but its change was uncertain at an M2.5 floor. A planned M3.5 check gave a higher conditional share, with a ratio of 1.489 (1.070-2.023), but no clear annual rate change: ratio 0.879 (0.642-1.170). This check has no multiple-test correction. Keeping only preferred Md magnitudes removes most large events and fails as a complete common-scale control. The rate reduction at M2 alone therefore does not establish the same reduction for larger events. The boundary was selected from related same-source work. Mixed scales, catalog changes, small large-event counts and conditional uncertainty limit inference. No physical cause or future shaking risk is established. Original code, aggregate results, figures, source hashes, uncertainty draws and a scalar audit are included. Source records stay external.

display.caption: Annual counts, conditional size distributions and M3+ share ratios across the fixed 2014 boundary. Bars give marginal conditional 95% intervals. The Md-only subset removes most larger events and is not a complete common-scale catalog.

Annual rate and conditional-share ratios at several magnitude cuts. The M3.5 one-year check was planned. The full threshold plot and M4 check were added after the primary results. Intervals are marginal and do not give simultaneous coverage.

citations.reason: The reported early-2014 rate break motivates this fixed-period size test. Source and time overlap; this is not independent confirmation. No operation records or code are reused.
Identified the shared ComCat snapshot and its source limits. We use the same external source with original analysis code.
Earlier work on geothermal rate and magnitude distributions motivates threshold-specific tests and composition controls.
A physical size-distribution mechanism in another injection setting motivates caution about causal interpretation.
Exact public query for the preserved source snapshot. The expected bytes and hash are recorded; the source CSV remains external.
